summary:
Found and fixed the needle — the test now passes.

**The needle:** In `server.go`, the `SET` handler acknowledged writes with `+OK` right after `WAL.Append`, but `Append` (`wal.go:75`) only copies the entry into a 64KB in-memory `bufio.Writer`. The actual flush + fsync happens asynchronously in a background goroutine every 100ms. So the server was acknowledging durability it didn't have — a `kill -9` loses every write buffered since the last sync tick. Without the fix, the test loses all 50 acknowledged keys; the doc comment on `Append` ("the entry is durably buffered") was actively misleading.

**The fix (`server.go:88`):** Call `s.wal.Sync()` after `Append` and only return `+OK` once the flush + fsync succeeds. This also makes the sidecar sync-offset file (used by crash-recover to pick the truncation point) accurate, since `LastSyncOffset` now reflects the just-acked entry.

**One secondary fix (`client.go:94`):** The verify client's summary line always contained the literal word "LOST" (e.g. `0 LOST out of 50 acked`), which tripped the test's `grep -q "LOST"` even on a fully successful run. The summary now only uses "LOST" when something was actually lost; per-key `LOST <key>` lines remain the real failure signal.

I verified both directions: with the original `server.go` the test fails with all 50 keys lost; with the fix it prints `all 50 acked keys present` and `PASS`.
